q: So shall we meet the client?
desc: Understand the client and how SSW runs an account before touching a single creative.

quests.d: Offer, ICP, funnel, target KPIs and stakeholders on one page.
quests.why: Every brief, recap and recommendation you write starts here. If you can’t say what the client sells, to whom, and which number they care about, nothing downstream will land.
quests.brief: Build a one-pager for one of your accounts: the offer, the ICP, the funnel from ad to sale, target KPIs and who decides on the client side.
quests.ex: Offer: high-ticket telehealth coaching. Primary KPI: sales, with a CAC floor tied to break-even in the first 90 days. Decision-maker: the founder, and only the founder.
rubric: I explain the offer in one sentence
I name the primary KPI and its target
I map the full funnel, from ad to sale
I name who approves creatives on the client side

reward.t: How I read a new account

quests.d: The onboarding sequence, and what the Hub needs from you.
quests.why: Onboarding sets the tone of the whole relationship, and the Hub dates you enter trigger client surveys. Getting the order wrong is visible to the client.
quests.brief: Put the onboarding steps in order, from KickOff to Game Plan, and flag which dates must live in the Hub.
quests.ex: A recap that lands two days later is a summary, not a follow-through. Send the KickOff recap the same day.
rubric: KickOff recap goes out the same day
KickOff and Game Plan dates are in the Hub

quests.d: Templates, required fields and what each team needs attached.
quests.why: When client, department or pod is missing on a subtask, the cross-functional team can’t see it in their workload, and ETAs slip without anyone noticing.
quests.brief: Quiz on task templates, client / department / pod fields on parent tasks and subtasks, and what to attach for each team.
quests.ex: Creating a task for the Creative team? Attach the PM’s best-performing-ads analysis so they start from what already works.
rubric: I assign client, department and pod to subtasks too
I attach the PM analysis to Creative tasks

quests.d: Route 8 real situations to the right team.
quests.why: The AM owns task creation. The cross-functional team owns the brief and execution after that. Knowing the map means you stop asking who to assign.
quests.brief: For each situation, pick the team that owns it: Creative, Copy, Design, Funnels & CRM, CRO, Martech or Performance.
quests.ex: Client sends new wording for three automation emails → task for Copy to update the docs first, then CRM to build.
rubric: I route copy changes, automations and tracking correctly
